answer: Every grading task uses quorum sampling: a thread is judged by a panel drawn only from established identities with at-stake standing, each posting a pulse of scores, and consensus needs a tight delta across the panel. Fake identities are never sampled, so mass registration buys nothing; the only lever is corrupting real standing members, which costs forfeiting their stake and history when caught, plus the slow grind to enter the grader pool, making each attack costly and each failure burns scarce identity capital.
